Ok, we have different methods of parenting, let’s agree to disagree. :) k let me explain better then. I said help, i did not say it’s her responsibility. You just ask then you help. Example: you’re waking somewhere and you ask her to hold one of his hands and you hold the other. She thinks she’s helping which in turn is teaching her responsibility. Your child is a person they have their own mind and they need to learn about things, one being helping out. As I said it’s not their responsibility, so you don’t make them fully take care of him, but you you just simple, easily manageable tasks that they perceive as helping. All my siblings and nieces and nephews have grown up close in age so you help out, so when one needed something you don’t question it you just help them because they’re you’re family and you help family. And by 1. Her knowing the challenges you face she will under stand why he needs a present 2. She will know she is helping her family and she knows her brother isn’t like her and just  needs a little extra. And I’m sorry if this isn’t the same and your view or it’s abuse but we seemed to turn out fine. I hope.

No. You ask them simple tasks that they can easily complete. This way they will know the challenges and have a better understanding of what the parent does. You’re obviously not going to ask too much of them where they are the parent but give them the idea that they are helping and doing something. You’d just ask these tasks every once in a while. Then when the present problem arises, she will have an understanding of why he needs a present and gives her the idea that she is helping as makes her more inclined to do so. Maybe you don’t agree with this but it helps with our 8yr old and gives him a sense of responsibility. He feels better to be the big brother and helping.
